caption: Segmentation and own uncertainty of every method on Replica office\_4 (frame 29) and ScanNet scene0070\_00 (frame 46). Each scene is our best test scene of its dataset, a favorable case: the largest per-scene mIoU margin of ours P2 over the best other row of Table~\ref{tab:replica}. Each frame is the evaluation frame with the most ground-truth classes that cover at least 0.5\% of its labeled pixels, a rule on the labels fixed before rendering. Row 1: the 3DGS render and the labels (black: no decision); row 2: the ground truth and the errors (vermillion: wrong; black: not scored); row 3: each method's own uncertainty, NormLift's $1-C_{\mathrm{inter}}$, the learned $u$ of LEGaussians and our $u^{\mathrm{ale}}$, as its rank among the covered labeled pixels with a defined value in all evaluation frames of the scene (grey: undefined; black: not covered). The 2D features and Feature 3DGS have no own uncertainty (-- in Table~\ref{tab:replica}); we show no P2 confidence. Numbers are per-scene values over all evaluation frames, read from Table~\ref{tab:replica}: mIoU (row 1) and the AUSE of the own uncertainty (row 3), in \%. LEGaussians $\lambda_u$ = 4 (Replica), 1 (ScanNet), chosen on validation. On office\_4, ours has the highest mIoU (35.2). On office\_4, NormLift's $1-C_{\mathrm{inter}}$ ranks the errors slightly better than $u^{\mathrm{ale}}$ (AUSE 4.6 vs 4.9). On scene0070\_00, ours has the highest mIoU (62.0). On scene0070\_00, $u^{\mathrm{ale}}$ has the lowest AUSE of the own uncertainties (5.2 vs 6.0, 10.2).
